thread_text:
lina: Heads-up -- we started a gated bring-up for comet-q1 (PTQ int8) against the golden-toolcall corpus. Early metric: structured-parse success drops from 99.97% (fp16) to 99.10% (int8). Not huge but visible.

sam: saw samples. Failures cluster on weird control bytes and long embedded arrays in the kv_prefix. Example emitted by model: `{"tool":"append","args":["meta","\u0007\u0000\u001b"]}` which our JSON parser rejects.

noah: thought: instead of broad sanitizer, could we run a delta gate that only applies a soft-rewrite for corpus members that historically parsed? i.e., if the original parse succeeded in golden-run, then we try a non-destructive rescue on the int8 emit.

lina: interesting. That avoids changing behavior for producers that rely on raw bytes. How would rescue look?

sam: prototype: attempt parse, if it fails, run two heuristics in order: 1) escape non-printables in string tokens and reserialize 2) wrap top-level emission in a single-field envelope if trailing truncation suspected. If either succeeds, mark as "rescued" and surface as a telemetry event.

triage-bot: note: added ticket ML-7893 to track rescue heuristics experiment and linked to canary dashboard.

noah: we need acceptance criteria: rescue shouldn't increase false-positive passes where semantics change. Suggest: run the full integration suite that hits binary-arg integrations and compare goldens. Also run a targeted delta-detection: diff canonical outputs and compute semantic equality (tool + arg identity). If rescue changes arg bytes, flag as induced-diff.

lina: ok plan: 1) implement rescue behind flag `rescue_parse_nonprintable` 2) run 50k replay across golden corpus (mirror mode) 3) collect counts: parse_fails_before, parse_fails_after, rescues, induced_diffs.

sam: started small job locally. Quick snippet of the rescue pseudocode I used:

```
if parse(emitted): return success
else:
  escaped = escape_nonprintables(emitted)
  if parse(escaped): emit_metric('rescued_escape'); return success
  envelope = try_envelope_fix(emitted)
  if parse(envelope): emit_metric('rescued_envelope'); return success
  return fail
```

noah: when you run the mirror, also compute divergence by hashing (tool + args) before/after; we want a list of changed keys to inspect manually. If >0.05% induced_diffs we fail the experiment.

lina: what about retry policies? current default retry_budget=1. If rescue reduces visible parse fails, maybe we can keep retries low. But for onboarding we could bump to 2 for canary to reduce noise while we observe. Thoughts?

sam: bumping retry_budget just hides regressions from metrics; prefer to keep it unchanged and use rescue telemetry to justify a controlled rollout. For customer-facing hosted, keep default. For dedicated/private we can document the flag.

ops-bot: deploy: comet-q1-int8-gate rolled to mirror nodes at 12:42; conservation of traffic enabled.

lina: I'll land the PR behind the flag and include a small evaluator that computes the induced-diff rate and emits a CSV summary. Tagging `eng-runtime` and `eng-ml`. If mirror pass < 0.02% induced diffs and parse_fails drop by >=80% we promote.

noah: add a follow-up to record examples of rescued-but-different emissions for the product/solutions team so they can advise customers that rely on binary args.

sam: linking replay job: https://replay.internal/jobs/2245 (queued). Will paste summary here when done.

lina: thanks all. reconvene in this thread after replay finishes.

(ops-bot will post job completion and metrics into thread)
